//: On, and what it took to turn it on is worth writing down.
The tests share scenario output trees: one converts and another reads what it wrote.
Reading together is fine, because a conversion is memoised per scenario and nothing
rewrites a tree it did not make. Building together was not: three attempts failed with
52, then 18, then 65 tests, and the set was different every run.
It was never a list of races. It was one property - a build directory was named after
the scenario, and a scenario belongs to no class. A dozen classes compile the `core`
output with a different harness beside it, and each of them cleared and rebuilt the same
folder. RepoLayout.WorkDir now names the calling test class as well, which is the unit
xUnit does not run against itself.
Three more, each its own kind of sharing: the check projects are one .csproj compiled
with a different GeneratedDir, so each build copies it (CsToolchain.ProjectCopy); the
conformance harnesses build inside the generated tree, which is the one place their
types are importable from, so those classes share a collection; and the updater servers
took a port between finding it free and binding it, so they retry.
And one that is not about building at all. A conversion that names environment
variables or extra arguments is not the shared one - it clears the scenario's tree and
writes a different one - so a class doing that is a writer among readers. `core` had
one, and it moved to the scenario that exists for it (`core-cli-side`); `core-server`
and `encrypted` have two classes each, which a collection settles. A new test that
converts with an option belongs to a scenario nobody else reads.
1,829 tests, 9m08s against 15m53s serial. doc/roadmap.md carries the same numbers.
